headline: Computational frameworks infer cell states and gene networks from single-cell data
label: Single Cell Computational Transcriptomics
summary: Recent preprints and publications extend single-cell transcriptomic inference to cell states, pseudotime geometry, memory genes and virtual perturbations.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational inference of cell identity, state transitions and regulatory structure from single-cell measurements. GmGM jointly infers cell-cell and gene-gene networks on a PBMC scRNA-seq dataset, and ClustoCell builds reference-free cell similarity graphs from within-cell expression tiers to recover cell types, states and markers. BIOCURRENT and PROFET reconstruct pseudotime geometry and continuous expression trajectories from transcriptomic and sparse time-series data, while Power-Seek infers memory genes from a single timepoint using a power-law signature in the cell covariance eigenspectrum. scGPA extends this logic to signed virtual knockdown. Remaining items apply related computational tools to nuclear morphology, fusion probe design, spatial copy number and Perturb-seq, and are heterogeneous in scope. What is new is inference that does not require lineage labels, replicates or multiple timepoints.
